questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to do my exchange in Amsterdam, as I have always wanted to get to know the city. It is a very nice city, and is also very much like copenhagen - i didnt want the biggest "culture chok" i just wanted to try something new

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy - it was just an entrance and i already had the information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: All uni-housing is off campus

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its far away from the centre

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In Amsterdam: if you get the chance of student housing, no matter what size or location - TAKE IT

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Confusing

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you would find courses, and them ask for them in your forhåndsgodkendelse, then you needed them to approve in OLA, and then you had to apply in "Glass" in where you were not able to get all the courses you wanted?

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: only guides, that didnt work

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: okay

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the guides

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
At UCPH i am registered at Humanities, however i was placed at social and behavioral sciences at UvA. 
I study Communication and IT, and I was not allowed to take any IT or computer science courses. A lot of the communication courses available in fall semester, we had already had, and those available for us were all on the same time. 
I ended up with a lot of sociology courses, which i had little to none prior experience in, which made it a lot harder also.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
For me, they were quite hard, but maybe thats because i didnt have courses in my field of study.
However, i would say that the study level is quite easy BUT (!!!) the work load is much harder

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
This is completely different. Almost every class is mandatory; there is attendance. 
Reading reports, assigments, quizzes ect.. every week.
I would compare the teaching style with a danish high school.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Digital Cultures: Interdisciplinary Perspectives
Introduction to Gender and Sexuality Studies
Social Trends, Social Problems & Social Policies
Urban Places & Social Problems

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
if i had to choose one then: Global Digital Cultures: Interdisciplinary Perspectives

However the exam is nothing like danish exams

questions.answer: All produce, cold cut ect. were cheeper than DK, however, the meat was a lille more expensive. All in all is Amsterdam cheeper than DK

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the ESN

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Have fun with your friends (that you will most likely find at your housing) and enjoy it while you can !!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Dutch people are like the danish. They like their own kind. I would go to local bars or clubs to interact with them, however, i would highly recommend finding other international students or expads !

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Only language

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everyone mostly minds their own business

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) ONLY take courses in your own field

2) look out for attendance

3) if there is attendance: have thursdays and fridays off for trips ect.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont go if you think it would be easy. The workload is maybe 3x as hard as UCPH

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Gaining an international network of beloved friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Attendance, workload, exams ect.. 

I have never studied so hard (both in high school, when i went to CBS or at KU) to just get "okay" grades...

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: other that the academics. i LOVED it !! 8/10 still

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
